figmaExecutionNotes: Desktop layout should be a single long-form landing page with clear vertical stacking and consistent 96px section spacing.
Use light theme throughout; avoid dark hero treatment because the product context does not call for trust-authority styling.
Apply Techjockey voice in microcopy only through structure and trust emphasis; do not add new marketing claims.
Keep trust/logos section above all feature content because the proof strategy explicitly prioritizes logos.
Mobile should mirror the same 5 sections in the same order, with single-column stacking for all feature grids and full-width stacked CTAs in the hero.
No pricing, testimonials, form, or news sections should be added because they are not supported by the input.
Use the default font pairing for collaboration products: Plus Jakarta Sans headings and Inter body.
Because hero headline is 18 words, keep it at the smallest hero tier from the memory rules to maintain layout stability.
Use actual content as-is; do not expand or rewrite feature descriptions beyond minor line breaks for Figma readability.

heroStrategy.headline: Elevate Your Team’s Productivity with Zoho Workplace
heroStrategy.subheadline: A Complete Email & Collaboration Suite for Enterprises that Facilitates Unified Communication.
heroStrategy.designNote: Hero should be an immersive full-width orange-led backdrop with a layered dashboard mockup slightly offset to the right, not a basic split layout. Use a gradient mesh with subtle grid lines and soft-shadow product cards to create depth. Keep the headline left-aligned in a large, confident type scale, with the CTA pair in brand accent styling. Place a logo trust band immediately below the fold so enterprise proof is visible fast. The visual should feel operational, premium, and productivity-first.

repetitionBreakers: Hero uses a split, product-visual composition on a strong orange field.
Trust is a logo marquee directly after the hero to front-load credibility.
Product narrative shifts into a tabs-with-preview section to avoid static grids.
Features alternate into a spotlight-plus-grid block, then a horizontal integration marquee for visual variation.
Testimonials use a carousel because there are 5 quotes.
Pricing is presented as a centered highlighted card to reset rhythm before the final CTA.
No two consecutive sections share the same background treatment or visual density.
blueprint.pageTitle: Zoho Workplace for Enterprises | Unified Email, Collaboration & Productivity
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Zoho Workplace, a unified email and collaboration suite for enterprises. Improve communication, teamwork, and productivity with trusted business tools.

sections.backgroundTreatment: solid brand field with subtle radial glow and faint dashboard grid texture
sections.designNote: Content-first hero that answers the required continuity checks: headline clearly states this is Zoho Workplace, subheadline identifies it for enterprises, and the primary CTA is 'Get Started' in solid accent at full opacity. Right side should show a layered product dashboard shell with email, chat, docs, meetings, and a few floating proof chips. Keep the copy concise and match ad-message continuity.

Immediate credibility band with 3-6 recognisable enterprise logos in a smooth horizontal marquee. If exact brand logos are unavailable, use a logo-style strip and include the 'Trusted by 100,000+ Businesses Globally' proof as a compact anchor. Keep it visually dominant but not taller than a single trust row.

Use the first product block as the main explanation of how Zoho Workplace works in under 60 seconds: tabs for email, chat, docs, meetings, and storage with a live preview panel. This section should absorb the strongest click-driving features, especially unified workspace and real-time collaboration. The remaining product sections should not repeat the same structure; instead, transition into a spotlight-plus-grid module for feature depth and a horizontal integration marquee for app ecosystem breadth. Avoid static card-grid treatment for the 5+ integration features.
Because include=false, this section should be omitted from the visual hierarchy or reduced to a hidden/no-op block in implementation. Do not create a prominent section for it.

Proof section should emphasize enterprise confidence using the strongest available proof type. If logo proof is available, use it as the primary trust layer; if testimonial content is used, convert to a compact carousel rather than a grid because there are 5 items. Keep the tone operational and result-oriented, with short quote excerpts and role labels.

Present a single highlighted pricing card with the included enterprise-grade deliverables and migration assistance. Keep this section visually calm after the proof block, then bring the CTA back decisively. Primary button must be 'Get Started' in solid accent color only.

Final conversion block should be a centered floating card with a short reassurance-led form experience. Since the warm traffic sequence prefers CTA over hard sell, keep the form minimal and action-first. Mobile button should be full-width and use the same solid accent treatment.
Only use if extra media/logo content is needed; otherwise keep omitted. If shown, make it a low-height horizontal logo strip to close with additional credibility, not a content-heavy news module.

blueprint.designPersonality: A polished enterprise productivity system with warm brand energy: light surfaces, precise dashboard structure, strong logo-led credibility, subtle depth, and a clear sense of unified workflow efficiency.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a layered product composition: a clean Zoho Workplace dashboard shell on the right with email, chat, docs, and meeting widgets; float small proof chips like 'Trusted by 100,000+ businesses', support, and security markers around it. Add a marquee logo band immediately below the hero so customer logos become the dominant trust signal.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The hero headline is mid-length and needs to stay confident while fitting a split, dashboard-led composition without line breaks becoming awkward.

colours.colourReason: The brand palette already defines a strong orange identity, so orange becomes the hero background/primary CTA colour as instructed. White, charcoal, and soft grey create a premium light-theme enterprise feel while keeping the page clearly tied to Zoho Workplace and Techjockey branding.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Top-heavy split hero with brand logo lockup, large centered headline, concise supporting line, and a compact bullet-value proposition list; no explicit hero media visible in the provided markup.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-banner lead-in followed by a lead-capture form block and then stacked content sections; rhythm is linear and conversion-first with clear separation between promo, form, and feature narratives.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Form card and content sections appear as simple rectangular containers with utility spacing; no evidence of glassmorphism, shadow-heavy cards, or hover-elevated product cards in the provided markup.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary conversion is form-driven rather than button-driven in the visible HTML; use one dominant CTA path with a secondary offer CTA where needed, placed near the hero and repeated after value sections.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing pattern detected in the provided reference markup.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer not visible in the provided source; no footer pattern inferred.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Logo-first hero treatment with minimal media; if media is used, keep it secondary and aligned within a clean grid rather than as a full-bleed visual background.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Stacked feature sections with short labels, section headlines, descriptive lead text, and feature groups presented as compact blocks; best suited to progressive disclosure and scannable benefit lists.
referenceMap.formPattern: Embedded lead form card directly under the hero, using hidden tracking fields and a visible form header; treat as a high-priority conversion module with minimal friction and strong proximity to the promise above.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No explicit animation system is evident from the provided markup; interaction should remain lightweight and largely static unless added by external scripts.
designNotes: Prioritize conversion clarity over storytelling depth.
Keep hero messaging short and benefit-led.
Use compact bullet lists to communicate proof points quickly.
Maintain strong vertical hierarchy with one primary action path.
Favor simple content containers over decorative card treatments.
Use clear separation between hero, form, and feature sections.
If adding visual motion later, keep it subtle and non-essential.

mustHaveMoments: Prominent trusted-by logo/social proof strip above the fold
Concise value proposition focused on unified communication and productivity
Compact CTA pair for immediate conversion action
Feature-led sections that reinforce all-in-one collaboration benefits
Pricing/inclusions block with clear plan value
Testimonial section to support purchase confidence
avoidPatterns: Heavy hero media that dilutes trust signals
Long-form storytelling before proof and CTA
Overly playful visuals or copy that reduce enterprise credibility
Multiple competing CTAs in the same viewport
Dense comparison tables that slow the single-product journey
designStrategy.reasoning: This is a single-product, enterprise-oriented landing page for a solution-aware audience, so the page should push qualified leads toward trial/start actions rather than educate from scratch. Because the visitor trusts logos most, the strongest conversion lever is a logos-first proof hierarchy placed immediately in the hero and repeated before deeper sections. The content already includes strong enterprise utility messaging, pricing inclusions, and testimonials, which supports a proof-led narrative. A split hero is ideal for balancing clear messaging with trust elements while keeping the light-theme layout clean, efficient, and conversion-focused.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
